cards.text: Judah's got a new king, friend: Zedekiah, twenty-one years old, put on the throne in Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, who also renamed him (2 Kings 24:17). A crown AND a new name from the same guy? All I ever got was a name, and the Millers had to CARVE it into my handle.

cards.question: So what kind of king is Zedekiah? True or false: he does evil in the sight of the LORD, just like Jehoiakim, an earlier king of Judah.

cards.text: Then the writer gives the big picture: "…because of the anger of the LORD, all this happened in Jerusalem and Judah, until He finally banished them from His presence."

cards.question: Zedekiah owes his throne to the king of Babylon. What does Zedekiah do to him?

answers.text: He makes a treaty with him

cards.text: Rebelling against the man who gave you your NAME is like telling off your boss while wearing the name tag he printed for you. So in Zedekiah's ninth year, Nebuchadnezzar marches against Jerusalem with his entire army.

cards.question: Nebuchadnezzar's army camps outside Jerusalem and builds a siege ___ all around the city.

cards.text: And the siege doesn't let up. It drags on until King Zedekiah's eleventh year.

cards.question: After all that time under siege, Jerusalem still has plenty of food by the ninth day of the fourth month.
Then Jerusalem is breached, with the Chaldeans, Babylon's army, surrounding the city. What do Judah's men of war do?

cards.text: They slip out through the gate between the two walls, near the king's garden, and head toward the Arabah. Tiptoeing past an army in the dark, I'd hold my breath so hard my mustache would go stiff.

cards.question: King Zedekiah and his men of war have slipped out of Jerusalem in the dark. What does the Chaldean army do?

cards.text: The Chaldeans overtake King Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho.

cards.question: When the Chaldeans catch up to King Zedekiah, his whole army stands and fights beside him.

cards.text: Deserted by every last soldier. The Chaldeans seize Zedekiah.

cards.question: The Chaldeans bring King Zedekiah up to the king of Babylon at ___.

cards.text: There at Riblah, the Chaldeans pronounce judgment on Zedekiah. Friend, I think this part hurts.
They slaughter Zedekiah's sons before his eyes. Then they put out his eyes.

cards.question: The Chaldeans bind King Zedekiah with bronze shackles. Where do they take him?

cards.text: Babylon isn't done with Jerusalem. On the seventh day of the fifth month, Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard and a servant of the king of Babylon, enters the city.

cards.question: Nebuzaradan is inside Jerusalem. What does he do to the house of the LORD?
Nebuzaradan spares the royal palace and the houses of Jerusalem.

cards.text: Then the whole Chaldean army under him breaks down the walls around Jerusalem. Even the junk drawer I lived in still had all four of its sides.

cards.question: With Jerusalem's walls down, what does Nebuzaradan do with the people left in the city?

answers.text: He makes them rebuild the walls

cards.question: But Nebuzaradan leaves behind some of the ___ of the land to tend the vineyards and fields.

cards.text: Then the Chaldeans strip the house of the LORD of its bronze, gold and silver and carry it all off. King Solomon built that house (1 Kings 6:14), and the bronze from his two pillars, the Sea and the stands alone was beyond measure. Each pillar stood eighteen cubits tall.

cards.question: Besides the treasure, Nebuzaradan takes some people. Which of these does he take?

cards.text: From those still in the city, he also takes a court official over the men of war, five royal advisors, the army captain's scribe and sixty more men. Nebuzaradan brings them all to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
There at Riblah in the land of Hamath, the king of Babylon strikes them down and puts them to death.

cards.question: When it's all over, Judah is taken into exile, away from its own land.

cards.text: Don't hang up that apron yet, friend. Judah's far from home, but this story still has pages left.
